summary: A request from Vint Cerf and Jon Postel at UCLA for a list of the well-known sockets used by network services at each host. They wanted to pick a standard socket for a Discard service and needed to know which were already taken. It notes that socket 1 was the Network Logger used for the Initial Connection Protocol, and asks each site's technical liaison to report their service sockets.

plainLanguage.summary: Before choosing a socket number for a new service, the authors want to know which numbers hosts already use. They ask hosts to send in a list of their service sockets.

subtitle: A request for each host to report socket numbers used by its network services.

tldr.problem: The Network Measurement Group wanted a standard socket for a Process Discard service but did not know which socket numbers were already allocated.
tldr.mechanism: The authors ask each Host Technical Liaison to provide the functions and socket numbers of network service programs at that host.
tldr.outcome: The note says socket 1 is the Network Logger, where ICP may be performed, and proposes maintaining a published catalog at the NIC.

sections.title: Finding an Available Socket
sections.content: The Network Measurement Group wanted to establish a standard socket number for a Process Discard service. It did not require every host to cooperate, but the group needed to know which sockets already served standard network functions.
sections.plainLanguage: The group wanted a socket number for a new service. First it needed to find out which numbers were already in use.

sections.title: The Request for Host Lists
sections.content:
RFC 322 states that socket 1 is the Network Logger at hosts that permit login for services, and that the Initial Connection Protocol may be performed there. The authors ask each Host Technical Liaison to report service functions and socket numbers.

They propose publishing the resulting catalog and recommend keeping it at the Network Information Center.
sections.plainLanguage: The note names socket 1 for the Network Logger and asks each host to identify its other service sockets. The proposed list would be published for the network community.

sections.title: A Request, Not a Protocol
sections.content: The RFC contains no specification for the Process Discard service and no completed catalog. It is a request for information from hosts, with contact details for the authors at UCLA.
sections.plainLanguage: This RFC asks hosts to send information. It does not define the new service or provide the catalog's final contents.
